articles.title: Man accused of assaulting boy, 14, at TTC subway station
articles.summary: Toronto Police Service (TPS) officers have made an arrest after an investigation into an alleged assault at a downtown subway station. Officers were called to College Station in the College and Yonge streets area at around 6 p.m. on Wednesday. Investigators say a 14-year-old male and the accused were on the same subway train. articles.summary: The Durham Regional Police Service (DRPS) has arrested 12 men after a “proactive human trafficking enforcement initiative” dubbed Project Firebird that was carried out in October. articles.title: Wire embedded in gummy candy, sewing needle found in Halloween haul in Durham Region: police
articles.summary: Durham Regional Police are urging parents to inspect their children’s Halloween candy after two separate reports of possible candy tampering in Ajax and Pickering. Investigators say the incidents were reported after families discovered foreign objects while sorting through candy collected during Halloween trick-or-treating on Oct. 31. articles.title: Weekend need-to-know: Royal Winter Fair returns
articles.summary: Despite the warmer weather, the Royal Winter Fair is back at Exhibition Place. Keep in mind, there will be closures on the TTC and GO Transit if you are heading across the city. articles.title: 2 arrested, police searching for suspect after Mississauga apartment building allegedly set on fire twice
articles.summary: Police say they have arrested two people and are searching for a third in connection with two fires at a Mississauga apartment building that they allege were deliberately set.

articles.title: Lady Gaga, Shakira, Jack White and Boy George lead the 2027 Songwriters Hall of Fame nominees
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — Lady Gaga, Shakira, Pink, Boy George, Jack White, Sia, Vince Gill, Ne-Yo, Blondie's Debbie Harry and Chris Stein and many more are among the impressive list of nominees for the 2027 Songwriters Hall of Fame class, an especially eclectic mix of pop, hip-hop, Latin, funk and rock innovators.

articles.title: 2 arrested, 1 sought in alleged targeted arsons at Mississauga apartment building
articles.summary: Peel Regional Police (PRP) have arrested two people and are searching for a third female suspect in connection with two arson investigations that allegedly targeted the same victim in Mississauga. Police say on Sept. 20 and Sept. 21, fires were deliberately set in a third-floor hallway of an apartment building in the area of Lakeshore […]

articles.title: Bingo, Care Bears, Pokémon cards and the classic playground slide make it into the Toy Hall of Fame
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — Bingo, Care Bears, the Pokémon Trading Card Game and the humble playground slide have all made it into the National Toy Hall of Fame, taking their place alongside classics like Mr. Potato Head and G.I. Joe.

articles.title: U.S.-made pipes are being installed next to Ontario's legislature as Canadian steel jobs vanish
articles.summary: As Canadian governments push to improve local supply chains amidst an ongoing trade war with the United States, the City of Toronto has been forced to head south of the border. Officials say only American companies make the steel pipes they are currently installing near Queen's Park.

articles.title: Amazon workers in Toronto area launch organizing drive with help of Unifor
articles.summary: A group of Amazon employees packed a hall in Scarborough on Wednesday to launch an organizing drive across fulfillment centres in the Greater Toronto Area with the help of Canada's largest private sector union.

articles.title: Woman dead after being struck by vehicle in Newmarket, police say
articles.summary: A woman in her 20s has died after being struck by a vehicle in Newmarket, Ont., on Wednesday evening, police say.

articles.title: Canadian military flying ace William Barker commemorated with new statue on Yonge Street
articles.summary: A new statue of a Canadian World War I flying ace was unveiled in Toronto Wednesday afternoon, the latest effort to breathe life into his memory, which his grandson said was nearly lost to time.

articles.title: Incoming Mississauga mayor pushes for provincial funding during first Queen's Park visit
articles.summary: During his first visit to Queen's Park since being elected mayor of Mississauga, Alvin Tedjo says he's pushing for more financial support from the province to help him address some key priorities.

articles.title: Ex-secretary of Serbian Orthodox Diocese of Canada charged with fraud over missing $200K: Halton police
articles.summary: The ex-secretary of the Serbian Orthodox Diocese of Canada, located in Milton, Ont., has been arrested and charged with fraud after a police investigation found over $200,000 went missing from the diocese.

articles.title: Early childhood educators call out Ontario over wage freeze, while child care capped at $22 until 2027
articles.summary: Early childhood educators called out the Ford government at Queen's Park Wednesday after a recent memo revealed a wage floor freeze and that workers will not receive an expected annual $1-per-hour increase in 2027.

articles.title: Man dead following industrial incident in Scarborough: police
articles.summary: A man is dead after an industrial incident that happened just before noon Wednesday near McNicoll Avenue and Tapscott Road, Toronto police say.

articles.title: 'There's no 2.0': Ford dismisses Toronto's bid for new funding agreement
articles.summary: Ontario Premier Doug Ford says he won't be signing a formal new funding agreement with the City of Toronto, even as city hall pitches for long-term help from Queen's Park. Ford, however, did signal some money could be unlocked for public safety.
